jobs.title: Minor League Complex Hitting Analyst and Rehab Coach
jobs.description:
DEPARTMENT OVERVIEW:   
The Player Development department is dedicated to fostering the comprehensive growth of our minor league players. Our mission is to excel in optimizing talent and skill development while aligning with player and team objectives. Our approach involves the creation of world class player programs and efficiently scaling them across our player pool. Collaborating closely with baseball analytics, performance, and medical, we establish effective frameworks for experimentation and learning. Additionally, we work closely with Amateur Scouting, International Scouting, and Pro Scouting to ensure seamless player transitions into the Red Sox organization.  
 
POSITION OVERVIEW:
The Complex Hitting Analyst & Rehab Coach will work closely with the Hitting Coordinator, Complex Hitting Coaches, and necessary auxiliary staff to support the daily needs of the hitting department. The role will be primarily responsible for building reports and tools using Snowflake and other available data sources, while also assisting with the daily execution of rehab hitting activities at the complex. 
 
As the Red Sox continue to build a team capable of being THE standard in player AND Staff development, we are looking for candidates who are organized, humble, proactive, and capable of communicating effectively across departments and levels of the organization.
 
The position is based out of the Player Development Complex in Fort Myers, FL. This position is seasonal, with full-time consideration for candidates with relevant experience. 
 Build and maintain reports, dashboards, and tools for the hitting department. Query and organize data from Snowflake to complete recurring and ad hoc requests. Work with Systems, Sports Science, and other departments to support hitting-related data needs. Identify opportunities to improve reporting, workflows, and access to information. Assist Complex Hitting Coaches with rehab hitters, including flipping, feeding machines, and throwing batting practice. Communicate relevant observations from rehab hitting activities to medical staff. Support additional projects and initiatives as assigned by the Hitting Coordinator. Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively across departments and levels of the organization. Experience working with Snowflake and SQL; experience with Tableau, R, Python, Excel, or similar tools is preferred. Prior experience operating in a hitting environment, including flipping, feeding machines, and throwing batting practice. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Humble, collaborative, and service-oriented. Demonstrates initiative, curiosity, and a willingness to identify and develop new solutions. Open-minded and eager to learn the organization’s hitting development processes and philosophies. In addition to the above requirements, all roles within Baseball Operations are expected to effectively demonstrate our universal competencies related to problem solving, teamwork, clarity of communication, and time management, along with embodying our culture of honesty, humility, relentlessness, and commitment to DEIB.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern, AI/ML Data Products
jobs.description:
ABOUT STRAVA

Strava is the app for active people. With over 200 million athletes in more than 185 countries, it’s more than tracking workouts—it’s where people make progress together, from new habits to new personal bests. No matter your sport or how you track it, Strava’s got you covered. Find your crew, crush your goals, and make every effort count. Start your journey https://www.strava.com/subscription with Strava today.

Our mission is simple: to motivate people to live their best active lives. We believe in the power of movement to connect and drive people forward.

As an Engineering Intern at Strava, you will be embedded in a team working on real projects that ship to our athletes and within the company, treated like a full-time member of the engineering team. You'll collaborate with cross functional teams that help us support and deliver to our athletes faster, while keeping them inspired and motivated.

We’ll give you experienced mentors and all the tools you need to make a meaningful impact on our product. To see examples of what past interns have contributed, read our Engineering Blog https://medium.com/strava-engineering! 



Available Internship:

 - Strava is looking for a Machine Learning Engineering Intern to join the Data Products team for Summer 2027.

 - The overall AI and Machine Learning team at Strava is responsible for sophisticated machine learning models and systems that power key Strava experiences, providing value to our athletes through personalization, recommendation, search, and trust and safety. This team also maintains the ML platform and infrastructure that lets us iterate on models quickly and deploy them reliably at scale.

 - This internship will specifically support the Data Products team, which sits at the core of Strava’s AI strategy, turning Strava’s unique community and activity data into reliable, reusable, enriched datasets that power experiences across the app. The team operates at the intersection of data engineering, ML platform engineering, and server engineering, building the pipelines and platform layer that let our proprietary embeddings, algorithms, and models reach athletes at scale. 



We follow a flexible hybrid model that requires you in our SF office four days per week.



What You’ll Do: 

 - Contribute to a focused project: Work with your mentor to pick and deliver a scoped piece of the Data Products team’s work. Depending on the team’s needs and your interests, this could be building a model that supports one of the team’s data products, designing an evaluation to measure how well our embeddings and models perform, or investigating a promising new dataset.

 - Experiment and analyze: Use Python, PyTorch, and SQL to explore Strava’s fitness and Geo data, run experiments, compare results against baselines, and document what you learn so the team can build on it.

 - Learn from the team: Work alongside machine learning engineers, data engineers, data scientists, and product managers, and pick up the practices that keep ML and data work reliable, like code review, reproducible experiments, and evaluation.

 - Share what you learned: Present your results to the team at the end of the summer. 



We’re excited about you because:

 - You have worked on machine learning problems through coursework, research, internships, or personal projects, and can break a problem down into incremental steps.

 - You write clear Python and have used tools like scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy, and PyTorch or TensorFlow.

 - You are comfortable with SQL and exploratory data analysis.

 - You understand core ML concepts such as supervised learning, train/validation splits, evaluation metrics, and overfitting.

 - You communicate clearly, ask good questions, and enjoy collaborating with people of all experience levels.

 - You are curious about deep learning, and about how fitness and Geo data can improve the athlete experience. 

 - You are currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Scienc

jobs.description: At Hudl, we build great teams. We hire the best of the best to ensure you’re working with people you can constantly learn from. You’re trusted to get your work done your way while testing the limits of what’s possible and what’s next. We work hard to provide a culture where everyone feels supported, and our employees feel it—their votes helped us become one of the Top 100 Inspiring Workplaces . We think of ourselves as the team behind the team, supporting the lifelong impact sports can have: the lessons in teamwork and dedication; the influence of inspiring coaches; and the opportunities to reach new heights. That’s why we help teams from all over the world see their game differently. Our products make it easier for coaches and athletes at any level to capture video, analyze data, share highlights and more. Ready to join us?   Your Role Cloud and software are among the largest investments we make, and for every dollar there is one that could also be going toward the product itself or the team building it. Our FinOps practice exists to make sure that spend is understood, accountable, and every dollar is working as efficiently as it can. On our team, you'll help own that picture. You'll allocate spend back to the services and teams driving it, forecast where it's headed, and consult teams on best practices to propose changes that maximize efficiency. You'll be a trusted partner to product and leadership on the real cost of what we build and what's on the roadmap, helping put those dollars to better use. We're hiring across experience levels, and your scope will grow with yours: you'll build, maintain, and improve our models and automation, and lead larger initiatives as you gain experience. As a FinOps Analyst, you’ll: Forecast and get ahead of cost. You'll build and maintain the models that track, allocate, and predict where our cloud and software spend is going, monitor AWS and the rest of our stack for anomalies, and action them the moment they surface. When something breaks, you won't just put out the fire, you'll help build the guardrails that keep it from starting again.  Turn spend into decisions leadership can act on. You'll maintain and improve the chargeback model that ties every dollar back to the service, squad, or contract that incurred it, and partner with Accounting and FP&A to keep the numbers aligned. When leaders have a question about cost, you're a trusted resource they come to. Automate anything worth doing twice. You'll use Python and SQL to take manual work off the team's plate, and work with GitHub Actions, Lambda, and DBT against our data warehouse. You'll also help manage AWS reservations and Savings Plans, and we'll teach you any tools that are new to you. If a task repeats, it's a candidate for automation, and you're the one who builds it. Find the work, then drive it home. You'll spot cost and efficiency opportunities, shape them into a pitch with support from teammates and stakeholders, and once approved, help carry them across engineering, product, finance, and accounting to completion. You're the connective tissue that keeps it all moving. Location Time spent collaborating with other Hudlies in-office will be a regular part of how you work. We’re currently prioritizing applicants  within commuting distance of Lincoln or Omaha, Nebraska. You’ll be expected to work more days in-office than remote, but will have the freedom to coordinate your specific in-office schedule with your team.  Must-Haves See the story in the numbers. You bring 2-5+ years of experience across data analysis, budgeting, and forecasting, or adjacent work such as revenue operations or business analytics, and you're just as comfortable digging into a trend as you are building a budget or projecting what comes next (Cloud FinOps context is a plus).
